sc: Bite on the foot in a field, swelling, gum bleeding, 20WBCT not clotted → Viper: polyvalent antivenom
Bite, ptosis, drooling, weak breathing → Cobra (neurotoxic): ventilate + antivenom
Child stung at night, sweating, vomiting, frothy sputum, cold hands → Scorpion pulmonary oedema: antivenom, prazosin, ICU
f: Reassure, immobilise the limb, remove rings · no tourniquet, cutting, sucking or herbal remedies · go to hospital
Local swelling · bleeding · 20-minute whole blood clotting test · ptosis, breathing · urine (dark) · observe ≥ 24 h
Indications: incoagulable blood, neurotoxicity, rapidly spreading swelling, shock · child dose = adult dose · repeat at 6 h if still incoagulable
Grade I: pain → local anaesthetic · severe: sweating, vomiting, priapism, pulmonary oedema → antivenom, prazosin 30 µg/kg
Wash 15 min · category III (deep, bleeding, face): vaccine + RIG · vaccine days 0, 3, 7, 14 · observe the dog 10 days
Bleeding, AKI · respiratory paralysis · compartment syndrome · tetanus · rabies (fatal once symptoms)
trap: The antivenom dose is the same for a child as an adult · a clotted 20WBCT at 24 h and no swelling = dry bite · fear of water after a dog bite = rabies
